vars.s: a pupil typing a report when the power goes off

worked_example.problem: Explain what happens to the work of {s} if it was not saved.
steps: While typing, the work is held in RAM.
RAM is volatile: it loses its contents when the power goes off, so unsaved work is lost.
Saving copies it to secondary storage (a disk or flash drive), which keeps it.
worked_example.answer: It is lost, because RAM is volatile; save often to secondary storage.

cards.idea: The CPU is the brain: the control unit directs, the ALU calculates.
RAM is volatile (loses data when power is off); ROM keeps its start-up instructions.
example: Save work so it is not lost.

cards.idea: Secondary storage keeps data permanently: HDD, SSD, flash drive, memory card, cloud.
example: A USB flash drive is easy to carry.
